issue.title: Status of testing Providers that were prepared on November 14, 2025
issue.body:
### Body

I have a kind request for all the contributors to the latest provider distributions release.
Could you please help us to test the RC versions of the providers?

The guidelines on how to test providers can be found in

[Verify providers by contributors](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/dev/README_RELEASE_PROVIDERS.md#verify-the-release-candidate-by-contributors)

Let us know in the comments, whether the issue is addressed.

These are providers that require testing as there were some substantial changes introduced:


## Provider [amazon: 9.17.0rc1](https://pypi.org/project/apache-airflow-providers-amazon/9.17.0rc1)

     Linked issues:

Hi @potiuk , I've test apache-airflow-providers-fab v3.0.2rc1 and it works! Here is the video proving that I can login and then logout successfully. https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Zut-Itvk7OAKs5liIrXsvVNdGI4gWXOi/view?usp=sharing and yeah, I won't use the RC version. Ok will wait the final version. Thank you very much for your work!

> I've test apache-airflow-providers-fab v3.0.2rc1 and it works!

Cool

My changes were focused around:

1. https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/57187
2. https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/57189

Both of those are non functional and they work as expected.

I have tested all my changes with Airflow==3.1.3:
#57541
#57894
#57143

I installed the pre-release provider packages and ran some DAGs. They successfully sent asynchronous notifications for Apprise and Slack.

For `apache-airflow-providers-common-compat`, I can confirm that the source code looks good.

However, there is a problem with the pinned dependency for
`apache-airflow-providers-apprise==2.2.0rc1`
`apache-airflow-providers-slack==9.5.0rc1`

they have
```
dependencies = [
    "apache-airflow-providers-common-compat>=1.8.0",
    ...
]
```

However, they both depend on the next version of `apache-airflow-providers-common-compat`, which is most likely `apache-airflow-providers-common-compat==1.9.0`.

That's how it should be

```
dependencies = [
    "apache-airflow-providers-common-compat>=1.9.0",
    ...
]
```

At that time I couldn't assign the dependency to a correct version because it hadn't been released yet. 

But can I just open a PR and change the dependencies? Although `apache-airflow-providers-common-compat==1.9.0` has not been released yet?

> At that time I couldn't assign the dependency to a correct version because it hadn't been released yet.

@dondaum  We've hit that chicken egg problem before, not sure if we've documented some best practice somewhere @potiuk ? I think the most important part is that you must set dependency in other providers to the next version of common.compat (so that it reflects the reality) and then actually bump the version of common.compat yourself in the provider.yml (and let the release manager know that you did that).
Not sure how to fix it now, will probably have to exclude those providers that rely on common.compat 1.9.0 ? and do an rc2? Let's wait for another opinion on that.

We can exclude those yes, and yes we have a proposed practice on that to comment that it will need next version of dependent provider so that the provider documentation preparation process will automatically bump the versions. We can definitely do that for rc2 round for those providers I will exclude them in this release round and will add both description of the proces and automation for the rc2 round

Most likely simply how it will look like is in project.toml, the contributor will need to add `# depends on next version` comment in the line with the dependency - that is what we tried already but without automation of actually bumping the version after seeing the comment.


How does that sound @kacpermuda  @dondaum ?

> We can exclude those yes, and yes we have a proposed practice on that to comment that it will need next version of dependent provider so that the provider documentation preparation process will automatically bump the versions. We can definitely do that for rc2 round for those providers I will exclude them in this release round and will add both description of the proces and automation for the rc2 round
> 
> Most likely simply how it will look like is in project.toml, the contributor will need to add `# depends on next version` comment in the line with the dependency - that is what we tried already but without automation of actually bumping the version after seeing the comment.
> 
> How does that sound [@kacpermuda](https://github.com/kacpermuda) [@dondaum](https://github.com/dondaum) ?

Thanks for your help @kacpermuda @potiuk Sounds good to me.

> Thanks for your help @kacpermuda @potiuk Sounds good to me.

Ok. I will test it myself (though it will be a bit dry-run as common-compat is already bumped) and will add some docs about it for the next vote (and automation). The **bit** of problem I have is how to catch those things during contribution. that's not an easy feat.  think current lowest dependency tests also install latest common.* providers, but maybe we should improve them to do some tests when the `common` providers are floored to the lowest version as well - that should catch vast majority of problems like that in the future.

For now: `apprise` and `slack` will be excluded and we will do rc2 with them. Let me know if there are other cases like that.

#57809 and #57446 are okay. There is a small problem with the first one [fix here](https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/58407), but it's a non-blocking one. I've added a new feature and one case is missing support, we can easily wait for next patch release.

Thank you everyone. Providers are released.

I will follow up with accelerated vote to `apprise` and `slack` providers - they were removed from that release - shortly.

I invite everyone to help improve providers for the next release, a list of open issues can be found [here](https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Aissue+label%3Aarea%3Aproviders).
